Tuning for the finite-rybar optimizer

Source: R/control.R
regsen_control.Rd

With rybar finite and cbar > 0, the DMP (2026) identified set has no closed form. Each bound is found by a global search over the unit cube (the DIRECT-L algorithm), followed by a local polish (Subplex) started from the point the global search returned. regsen_control() sets the budget of both. Pass the result to the control argument of regsen_bounds() or regsen_breakdown(); regsen_boot() and regsen_multi() hand it on through ....

Usage

regsen_control(maxiter = 1000L, polish = 300L, precision = 1e-08)

Arguments

maxiter

Maximum number of objective evaluations in the global search, per bound. Default 1000.

polish

Maximum number of evaluations in the local polish, per bound. 0 skips the polish. Default 300.

precision

Relative tolerance on the parameter point at which the global search stops; the polish uses one hundredth of it. Default 1e-8.

Value

A list of class regsen_control.

Details

The defaults agree to within about 3e-4 with a run twenty times as long on the bundled data. To check a result of your own, run it again with a larger budget, for example regsen_control(maxiter = 5000, polish = 1500), and compare: bounds that move by more than you care about mean the default budget is too small for your problem. The closed-form regimes (rybar = Inf, or cbar = 0) and the Oster analysis ignore these settings.

Examples

regsen_control()
#> <regsen_control> maxiter = 1000, polish = 300, precision = 1e-08
regsen_control(maxiter = 5000, polish = 1500)
#> <regsen_control> maxiter = 5000, polish = 1500, precision = 1e-08
